findings.claim: The recorded final_verify verdict for this unit is a stale REFUTED: it was folded from the pre-repair audit and pre-repair blind evidence, and neither verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl nor final_verify.jsonl was regenerated after the repair and the regate.
findings.evidence: reviews/final_verify.jsonl (mtime 14:02:49) — the only and therefore last line for las-b9-002 — reads verdict 'REFUTED', note 'gkey_records=4 ... audit=CONFIRMED_NOTES audit_major=1 audit_minor=3'. The audit it folded is audits/las-b9-002.json at mtime 13:56:12 (round 1). The repair landed afterwards: reviews/pedagogy.jsonl 14:09:03, shipping file candidates-final/las-b9-002.json 14:16:27. Fresh blind evidence was appended afterwards too: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl 14:11:44, verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl 14:11:53, verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl 14:12:31 (all four new lines executed_by '*-regate0726', all pass, solver_answer B and D). But verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl is still at 14:02:31 and contains only the four pre-repair G-KEY lines, so vfinal_fold.py's _last_wins over the resolved file cannot see the regate. Per vfinal_fold.py's fold rule, 'any non-minor audit finding' -> REFUTED, and majors is computed as `severity != "minor"`, so the single round-1 major alone pins the unit at REFUTED.
findings.why: vfinal_fold.py's docstring makes it the ONLY legitimate writer of final_verify records and a pure function of on-disk evidence; the evidence changed after the fold ran, so the ledger no longer describes the shipping file. Under last-line-per-stage-wins the unit is currently recorded REFUTED for a major that no longer exists in the file. Fix is mechanical: re-run gkey_resolve.py over verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-{1,2}.jsonl, then re-run vfinal_fold.py against this round-2 audit (all findings minor + CONFIRMED_NOTES -> VERIFIED_NOTES).

findings.claim: The q:1 C relabel replaced an in-taxonomy LÄS trap label with 'polarity_mirror', which is not in the LÄS trap set at all and is a defined ELF cloze label meaning something else — while the label the repair discarded, reversed_causality, is defined in this repo to cover exactly this swap.
findings.evidence: The LÄS trap taxonomy is closed at five labels: las/blueprint-template.md:95-99 and las/scripts/build_families.py:38-42 list reversed_causality, overgeneralisation, scope_shift, detail_as_main, plausible_worldknowledge. build_families.py:39 defines reversed_causality as 'Rätt element, fel riktning: orsak/verkan ELLER SUBJEKT/OBJEKT kastas om (textens tvärtom)' — q:1 C keeps the right elements and swaps which objection was the common one and which the rare one, i.e. the subject/object clause verbatim. 'polarity_mirror' is defined only in elf/blueprint-template.md:68 as an ELF trap: 'the positive-pole word where the contrastive frame demands negative (cloze signature)' — a lexical-cloze construct with no LÄS meaning. grep over every batch shows batches/batch9/candidates-final/las-b9-002.json is the ONLY LÄS unit in the pipeline that carries it. The contrast is instructive: 'stance_inversion' (used for q:2 A) is a legitimate documented LÄS extension — batch3/gen-las-short-1.NOTES.md:30-31 introduces it with an explicit rationale and it recurs in las-b3-002 and three batch4 units — whereas polarity_mirror was coined in a review note with no taxonomy entry. The label is also student-facing: the q:1 rationale reads 'C är polarity_mirror: ...'.
findings.why: Integrated checklist row 9 requires trap labels to name the actual trap, and family/trap accounting downstream (las/families.md, las/scripts/question_taxonomy.py, which has a reversed_causality regex matching 'kastar om'/'byter plats'/'tvärtom' and no polarity_mirror pattern) is keyed to the closed LÄS set. Two in-taxonomy fixes exist: keep reversed_causality on the strength of its own 'subjekt/objekt kastas om' clause, or coin the label properly the way stance_inversion was — a NOTES entry plus a taxonomy line — rather than borrowing a name that already means a different thing in the sibling ELF spec. Metadata-and-rationale-only, so not student-answer-affecting.
